clinician.trajectory_summary: A 9-year-old girl with a confirmed pathogenic p.Gln694Ter ZEB2 gene mutation diagnostic for Mowat-Wilson syndrome presented with visual pathway conduction disorders characterized by alternating convergent strabismus, astigmatism, and temporal pallor of the optic nerve discs. Initial ophthalmologic exam showed normal pupillary light responses, no eye movement limitation, and minor posterior synechiae. Cycloplegic autorefraction confirmed significant astigmatism. Ocular ultrasound demonstrated optic nerve drusen with increased echogenicity at the optic disc. Electrophysiologic (VEP) and brain MRI studies were ordered but results were not documented. Less than a year later, clinical progression was noted with worsening right eye object tracking associated with total cortical cataract in the right eye and partial cortical cataract in the left eye; pupillary reflexes remained normal. Follow-up ocular ultrasound confirmed increased echogenicity of the right optic nerve head and lens. Neurologically, the patient had psychomotor delay with no communication or walking ability and known callosal dysgenesis and ventricular dilatation on MRI. This multidisciplinary evaluation and genetic confirmation supports the diagnosis of Mowat-Wilson syndrome presenting with characteristic ophthalmologic and neurologic features.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: The patient is a 9-year-old girl with a pathogenic p.Gln694Ter mutation in the ZEB2 gene confirming Mowat-Wilson syndrome.
Initial exam showed alternating convergent strabismus without limitation in eye movements, normal pupillary responses, and pallor of the temporal optic nerve discs.
Cycloplegic autorefraction revealed significant astigmatism in both eyes.
Ocular ultrasound demonstrated increased echogenicity at the optic nerve head consistent with optic nerve drusen.
Less than a year later, the patient had worsening right eye tracking, total cortical cataract in right eye, partial cortical cataract in left eye, with persistent optic nerve pallor.
Neurological features included psychomotor delay with no communication or walking ability, callosal dysgenesis, and ventricular dilatation on MRI.
